note.question: How can a platform reserve finite resources effectively when customer contexts arrive adversarially and context-action consumption probabilities must be learned online?
note.overview: A platform allocates finite, nonreplenishable resources to sequential customers whose contexts can vary arbitrarily, while stationary context-action outcome laws must be learned from chosen-action feedback. IBOL combines a depletion-sensitive inventory-balancing potential with a bandit oracle, separating competitive loss from adversarial arrivals and regret from learning. The paper derives matching and segmented-recommendation variants plus a multiple-price assortment extension, with UCB, lazyUCB, and Thompson-sampling instantiations.

coverage.note: Core formulation, IBOL construction, parameter tuning, UCB and lazyUCB variants, performance guarantees, segmented recommendation, and the multiple-price hotel extension are mapped. Equations are Atlas-normalized restatements; proofs and ancillary literature are not reconstructed exhaustively.
